source: OECD (2025), Health at a Glance 2025: OECD Indicators, OECD Publishing, Paris
framing: Gap framing: every figure is what is NOT covered, NOT satisfied or unmet. Gap figures are 100 minus the published figure.
rule: HAL may phrase these facts freely but must not state any figure, ranking or claim that is not in this list. Verbatim report sentences may name other countries; only what they say about this country may be used.

facts.text: 29% of people in Australia were NOT satisfied with the availability of quality healthcare where they live in 2024, versus an OECD average of 36%; satisfaction has deteriorated over the past decade.
27.2% of health spending in Australia was NOT covered by government or compulsory insurance schemes in 2023, versus an OECD average of 24.9%.
32% of hospital care costs in Australia were NOT covered by public or compulsory schemes in 2023, versus 11% on average in the OECD.
13% of outpatient medical care costs in Australia were NOT covered by public or compulsory schemes in 2023, versus 22% on average in the OECD.
88% of dental care costs in Australia were NOT covered by public or compulsory schemes in 2023, versus 68% on average in the OECD.
52% of pharmaceutical costs in Australia were NOT covered by public or compulsory schemes in 2023, versus 42% on average in the OECD.
Duplicate private health insurance was most widely used in Australia and Ireland.
Australia and Israel also exhibit relatively high healthcare prices.
